verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md lines 29-36 (Core Workflow): '3. **Implement** - Write TypeScript components with proper types' ... '6. **Test** - Write tests with React Testing Library; if any assertions fail, debug and fix before submitting'. Constraints section (lines 120-137, MUST DO / MUST NOT DO) contains no rule about test ordering at all — no 'write tests first' and no 'do not implement before testing' either way. references/testing-react.md has zero mentions of TDD, red/green, or 'failing test' (grep confirmed empty). KICKOFF.md lines 569-571 (step 8): 'use the sprint-execution skill to execute PHASE/<NN>-<MM>-PLAN.md under the test-driven-development skill — write the failing tests first, then implement to green...'. Critically, sprint-execution's own SKILL.md line 131-132 already states: 'Skill injection: ... the subagent loads it itself ... follow its guidance for all work in this track' immediately followed by 'TDD-first is the default task contract. Every implementation task: write the failing test, watch it fail, implement, watch it pass, commit. Subagents follow the test-driven-development skill; the dispatch prompt says so explicitly.'
verdicts.reasoning: This is not a genuine contradiction. react-expert's numbered Core Workflow is a generic descriptive checklist for standalone use, not an enforced ordering gate — its own Constraints section (the skill's actual MUST/MUST NOT rules) says nothing about test sequencing, so nothing in react-expert affirmatively forbids writing tests first. The claim also proves too much: this exact 'Implement' (step 3ish) then 'Test' (later step) shape is the universal template across essentially every dev-kit domain skill — fastapi-expert, django-expert, csharp-developer, golang-pro, nestjs-expert, rails-expert, spring-boot-engineer, cpp-pro, java-architect, laravel-specialist, dotnet-core-expert all follow the identical pattern — confirming this is the deliberate shared shape for a domain skill's reference workflow, not a react-expert-specific defect worth carrying as a unique finding (the original claim itself flags systemic:false, which undercounts this). More importantly, sprint-execution (the actual orchestrating skill dispatched at step 8, always loaded alongside any lane/domain skill) already states explicitly and unconditionally that 'TDD-first is the default task contract' and that subagents follow the test-driven-development skill regardless of what the domain skill's own workflow enumerates — that is the operative enforcement layer, not react-expert. KICKOFF's step 8 text is therefore, at most, redundant with what sprint-execution itself already asserts, not compensating for a gap or disagreement in react-expert specifically. A subagent given both skills has no actual behavioral conflict to resolve: TDD is the explicit, separately-stated task contract; react-expert's workflow supplies domain patterns (what a good component/test looks like), not a competing ordering mandate. Refuted.
